Herd immunity works much like a digital firewall in computer security. Imagine a network of computers where a malicious virus tries to spread. If most of the computers are protected by security software, the virus has very few unprotected targets to infect. Consequently, it becomes difficult for the virus to jump from one computer to another, effectively stopping the spread. Similarly, in a population, if enough people are vaccinated or immune to a disease, the pathogen struggles to find new hosts, thereby protecting those who are not immune.
